subject.title: fix(ssrf): allow loopback for hostnames in allowedHostnames list (#101965)

question: Should this PR restore loopback DNS answers for all policy `allowedHostnames`, including hostnames promoted from `allowedOrigins`, or should any exception be scoped only to browser navigation after owner approval?
rationale: The implementation partially reverses a just-merged SSRF hardening decision while the linked issue is explicitly marked for maintainer product and security review, so automation should not choose the trust boundary.

options.title: Reject global loopback override
options.body: Require the PR to avoid changing the shared SSRF helper so allowed-origin trusted hosts cannot rebind to loopback again; any browser exception should be separately designed.

options.title: Approve a scoped browser exception
options.body: Permit a narrow browser-navigation-only exception with tests proving metadata/link-local and provider/fetch SSRF paths remain hardened.

options.title: Retire the old browser contract
options.body: Keep the merged SSRF hardening as intended behavior and update the browser navigation test or docs instead of relaxing the shared resolver.

recommendation.title: Reject global loopback override
recommendation.body: Require the PR to avoid changing the shared SSRF helper so allowed-origin trusted hosts cannot rebind to loopback again; any browser exception should be separately designed.

likelyOwner.reason: They opened the linked issue and have the strongest recent decision signal across the SSRF hardening and browser policy boundary.
